There's a book out there on Amazon called Airline Confidential. The title seems to imply that it contains the same gritty, inside look into the otherwise closed-to-public, code-to-access doors of the airline cockpit as Anthony Bourdain did with his look inside the professional kitchens of the world with his masterful, shocking, yet truthful and unembellished book, Kitchen Confidential. Unfortunately Airline Confidential is no such work of art or journalism. Instead it's a tiresome book that considers its cornerstone to be the repetitive telling of the tales of passengers' attempts to mash genitals together inside the unholiest of cubicles - the modern airline lavatory, in their quest to achieve their Mile High Club badges, get their adrenaline fix or save their plummeting mid-life mid-marriage libido crises. Multiple choice answers.

This is not an attempt to right such wrongs. And although I would in true Canadian form apologize to Bourdain this is not an expression of regret either. 'What you cannot explain about the world, you should at least attempt to describe' said somebody important, I'm sure. And herein I will attempt to describe the mostly ugly side of this post Golden-Age, post 9-11, post Recession-Economy, post North-American-Downturn regional airline. I will attempt to describe it instead of explain it because I have often found that an explanation implies that there are rational thought processes and reasonable men behind such a thing as an explanation and in extension behind a machine as mammoth as an airline. As you might come to see, I have found that this is not the case.

I like the CCP requirement to downvoat and want it to stay in place. If anything, I don't think I'd mind seeing it made even more stringent. And yes - I don't doubt that it already drives some users away, and if it was more stringent, would drive even more users away. Since the exact people it would drive away are those who resent having to post good content before being allowed to downvoat other people's posts, I count that as a gain for the site.

I'm less supportive of the initial upvoat limits, since I count shallow downvoating as more destructive than shallow upvoating, but I don't have a real problem with it.

The -50CCP automatic privilege revocation thing... I dunno.

In a way, I like it, since it puts the power in the hands of the community. It can't be denied that there are some users who are so thoroughly without any redeeming value that the site is better off without them, and I'd prefer that the users as a whole determine that than that mods or admins do. The problem though, presuming that the policy is desired, is that it has to be set up so that the privilege revocation can ONLY come about as a result of a pattern of behavior instead of one or even a few notably unpopular posts. I'm not sure if that's possible, though I'd think it would be with a system that tracked the ongoing pattern of up and downvoats a user receives instead of just the raw numbers. In any case, that's not the system that currently exists.

And I'm not really comfortable with the whole policy. Partly that's just a reflexive distaste for censorship. I don't really oppose the censorship of posters who demonstrably contribute nothing of any value to the site, but I don't like to open the door to censorship at all, and I think this policy does just that. And from a purely practical standpoint, I think it would be more effective - I know I'd prefer - to just let them keep posting and let the users who want to use the site without having their garbage impinge on them just block their accounts. It accomplishes the same thing in the long run - removes lousy content from the page of anyone and everyone who doesn't want to deal with it - but does it on a case-by-case basis, and without broadly censoring anyone. And, as a bonus, it would keep the useless posters to their own accounts, rather than having them just start an endless progression of new accounts, each one of which is inevitably going to end up crossing the threshold into privilege revocation anyway.

Yeah, I also find the -50CCP bar pretty low. A quite low amount of people/usernames can decide to silence a user. One part of a solution I read in another comment, was to at least subtract 1 CCP from your own account if you downvote another user's comment.

I find it a bit odd that there is a limit based on comment points but no ramifications based off of SCP; I suspect that will not always be the case. But I approve of the mentality that the community gets to regulate a bit - when you place all of the regulatory responsibilities on moderators, you allow a small group to decide (and it usually devolves into their own opinion) if a user should be silenced. I would be happy to see some anti-brigade mechanics, though, such as a moderator being sent a memo if a user has just downvoted 30 comments of a particular person, across multiple subs, in quick succession. Oh, and I'm still tossing around the idea of the CCP algorithm having a sort of mechanic to reflect, in part, recent behavior also instead of the account in its entirety.

Start by factoring out 1/x2 from the middle part to get

y'' = (1/x2)[x d/dx (dy/du) - dy/du]

Now we use the chain rule on the first term in brackets. Write

d/dx = (du/du) d/dx = (du/dx) d/du

Substituting this gives

y'' = (1/x2)[x (du/dx) (d2y/du2) - dy/du]

If manipulating differentials like that makes you uncomfortable, just remember that it really is the same thing as the chain rule and for many intents and purposes you can treat objects like dy/dx as if they were literal fractions.

Anyway, I'm pretty sure that the first line is telling us that du/dx = 1/x (if that isn't true, let me know; this would have been a substitution made earlier) in which case we obviously have x (du/dx) = 1 so the above equation is simply

y'' = (1/x2)[d2y/du2 - dy/du]

As required.
